data.name: Damor
data.gender_notes: Damor is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Damor is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘Dhanam’ which means wealth or prosperity. It is believed that the god of wealth, Lord Kubera, is often referred to as Damor. This name is said to bring blessings of wealth, prosperity, and abundance. The name Damor carries the meaning “God of Wealth and Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Damor usually hope their child will grow to embody god of wealth and prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Name of the god of wealth and prosperity
data.etymology: Damor belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Wealth and Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Damor total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Damor holds significant cultural importance in Hindu traditions. It is believed that bestowing a child with the name Damor will ensure a future of financial stability and prosperity. This name is often used in naming ceremonies and auspicious occasions.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Damor represents the divine blessing and grace of Lord Kubera, who is believed to be the god of wealth and prosperity. It is believed that invoking the name Damor will bring about financial abundance, with the underlying message being that true wealth lies not in material possessions but in the inner richness of one's soul.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Damor symbolizes the indestructible, unwavering, and unyielding divine power within an individual. It embodies the strength and resolve to overcome life's challenges, much like the unyielding Damodar river in Hindu mythology.

historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata mentions Damor as the name of a kingdom ruled by King Damanaka. It is located on the right bank of the Triveni River, which was believed to be a border between the Aryan and non-Aryan worlds. This reference likely dates to around 400 BCE.

Damor is also mentioned in the 13th-century Gujarati text, the Harshacharita, as a prominent port city. It was a significant trade hub during the medieval period, particularly for the trade of pearls, textiles, and spices.
